chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was in Kufa among you; every morning he would leave the palace early and circulate through the markets of Kufa, market by market. With him was a whip on his shoulder, which had two ends and was called 'Al-Sabayba'.

He would stop at the people of each market and call out: 'O group of merchants! Fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic!' When they heard his voice (peace be upon him), they would throw down what was in their hands, direct their hearts to him, and listen with their ears.

He would say (peace be upon him): 'Prioritize seeking Allah's choice (Istikhara), find blessings in ease, draw near to the buyers, adorn yourselves with forbearance, keep away from oaths, avoid lying, turn away from injustice, give justice to the oppressed, do not approach usury, fulfill the measure and the scale, do not deprive people of their goods, and do not wander in the land causing corruption.'
He would circulate through all the markets of Kufa, then return and sit for the people.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.السَّبِيبَةَ: A type of whip with two ends

ai.seo_question: What ethical advice did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) give to merchants in Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) active governance model in Kufa, where he personally inspected markets with the *sibbah* (a double-ended staff) to ensure justice and prevent exploitation. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the ruler's direct responsibility for economic ethics, linking commercial integrity to spiritual piety through specific prohibitions like *riba* and *ghish* (deception).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws was at Al-Kufa among you all, every day having breakfast early morning from the bread. So heasws would circle in the markets of Al-Kufa, market after market, and with himasws was a whip upon hisasws shoulder, and for it were two end bits, and it was called Al-Sabayba.

So he<sup>asws</sup> would pause at the people of each market, and he<sup>asws</sup> would call out: ‘O group of businessmen! Fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic!’ So whenever they heard his<sup>asws</sup> voice, they would throw down what was in their hands and they would hearken to him<sup>asws</sup> with their hearts, and listen to him with their ears’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> would be saying: ‘Procced with the Choice of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> (Al-Istikhara) and Blessings with the ease, and be closer to the buyers, and adorn yourselves with the forbearance and keep away from the oaths, and keep aside from the lies and the betrayals of the injustices, and do justice with the oppressed, and do not go near the interest (usury), and be loyal in the measuring and weighing, and do not belittle the things of the people and do not go around the land creating mischief!’
Thus, he<sup>asws</sup> would be circling in the entirety of the markets of Al-Kufa, then he<sup>asws</sup> would return, so he<sup>asws</sup> would sit (in judgement) for the people’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn Mahbub from ‘Amr ibn abu al-Miqdam from Jabir, who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, lived among you in al-Kufah. He would have one loaf of bread everyday for his lunch and walk in market-places of al- Kufah one by one with a durrah (whip) on his shoulder. It had two strips and it was called al- Sababiyah.

He addressed the people of every market-place and said, ‘Those people who do business must maintain piety before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’ People on hearing his voice dropped down whatever they had in their hands, their hearts repented and their ears listened.

He (the Imam) would say, ‘You must seek goodness (from Allah) and conclude a transaction with ease, stay close to buyers, dress up with forbearance, stay away from swearing, lying and injustice. Exercise fairness with the oppressed and do not become close to Riba’. Maintain proper measurement and balance. You must not reduce people’s things and you must not spread corruption in the land.’
He (the Imam) would walk in all of market-places of al-Kufah and then return to meet people.”
